outline.chapter_title: 1. Introduction to Long Context for LLMs
outline.description: Sets the stage for why extending the context window is important, outlines the limitations of existing LLMs, and previews the contributions of LongRoPE.
subtopics: Context windows in modern LLMs: size, importance, and challenges
Existing methods and their upper limits (~128k tokens)
Three main obstacles to further extension (catastrophic new positions, data scarcity, attention dispersion)
Overview of LongRoPE’s three innovations (non‑uniform interpolation search, progressive extension, short‑window recovery)

outline.description: Provides a refresher on positional encodings with a focus on Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE), setting the technical foundation for the whole chapter.
subtopics: Purpose of positional information in Transformers
RoPE mathematics and frequency formulation
Extension ratio and its effect on RoPE angles

outline.description: Reviews prior interpolation techniques (Linear PI, NTK, YaRN), their motivations, and limitations that motivate LongRoPE.
subtopics: Linear Positional Interpolation (PI) and its crowding problem
NTK‑based interpolation/extrapolation theory and limitations
YaRN’s frequency‑grouping approach and dependency on hand‑crafted thresholds

outline.description: Presents empirical findings that reveal two non‑uniformities—across RoPE dimensions and token positions—that are not exploited by prior methods.
subtopics: Evidence from evolutionary search experiments
Finding 1: RoPE dimensions need dimension‑specific scaling factors
Finding 2: Initial tokens benefit from reduced interpolation
Finding 3: Non‑uniform interpolation boosts both fine‑tuning & non‑fine‑tuning performance

outline.description: Describes how LongRoPE turns the interpolation problem into a search problem, details the search space, algorithm, and constraints that enable efficient exploration.
subtopics: Formulating the optimization objective over RoPE rescale factors
Defining the search space: λ_i and ℂoverline{n} ranges
Evolutionary search algorithm: population initialization, mutation, crossover
Monotonicity constraint on λ_i (lower dimensions smaller scaling)
Computational efficiency tricks (pre‑adding PI/NTK/YaRN seeds)

outline.description: Shows how LongRoPE’s search + fine‑tuning pipeline systematically reaches 2048k tokens without exhaustive training.
subtopics: Stage 1 – Search for 128k & 256k extensions from pre‑trained LLM
Stage 2 – Two‑step fine‑tuning: 400 steps at 128k then 600 steps at 256k
Stage 3 – Second search on the 256k fine‑tuned model to reach 2048k
Why this strategy is cheaper than direct 2048k fine‑tuning

outline.description: Explains the performance drop on the original window after extreme extension and how dynamic RoPE adjustment mitigates it.
subtopics: Crowding effect at high extension ratios
Secondary evolutionary search to recover 4k & 8k performance
Runtime switching of RoPE rescale factors during inference

outline.description: Details datasets, models, hyperparameters, evaluation tasks used to validate LongRoPE.
subtopics: Model choices: LLaMA2‑7B & Mistral‑7B
Fine‑tuning schedules (learning rates, batch sizes)
Search hyperparameters (population size, mutation rates)
Baselines: PI, NTK^2 , YaRN^2 , Code LLaMA , LongLoRA , etc.”],

outline.description: Presents key results across language modeling, retrieval tasks, and standard benchmarks illustrating LongRoPE’s advantages.
subtopics: Perplexity trends up to 256k tokens – comparison with baselines
Perplexity beyond 2000k tokens – success of 2048k extensions
Passkey retrieval accuracy up to millions of tokens
Zero/few-shot benchmark scores within original context window (“backward compatibility”)

outline.description: Investigates individual components of LongRoPE to understand their impact.
subtopics: Effectiveness of second positional interpolation vs. PI/YaRN
Benefit of short-context recovery step
Ablations on dimension-only vs. token-position-only vs. combined non-uniformities (effect sizes)

outline.description: Places LongRoPE among other strategies for long context handling.
subtopics: Retrieval-based approaches (memory modules) – tradeoffs with LLM architecture changes”],
